newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Howard calls for tax reform debate.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Howard calls for tax reform debate.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Wednesday there was need for an open debate on taxation reform for Australia.
"I believe we do need a debate on this issue," Howard said at a business forum in his home electorate in Sydney.

He said the three core objectives of any tax reform were to create more jobs, increase Australia's competitiveness and improve overall living standards. "If you are to compete effectively, the tax system must be up to world standards."
He invited representatives from business, welfare, academia and the public service to participate in the debate.

The Liberal/National government has been pressing recently for a major overhaul of the tax system, revising the push for a controversial goods and services tax (GST) that many blame for delaying the conservatives' return to power.
Howard promised before the March 1996 election not to introduce a GST, but has since qualified that promise by saying it applied only to its first term of government.
